results.input: Giải thích ngắn gọn sự khác nhau giữa relevance, recency và popularity của tool rank. Tôi chỉ hỏi cách sử dụng, chưa yêu cầu xử lý danh sách nào.

result.actual_text:
**Sự khác nhau giữa các tiêu chí trong tool `rank`:**

| Tiêu chí | Ý nghĩa | Khi nào dùng |
|----------|---------|--------------|
| **relevance** | Đánh giá mức độ liên quan của một mục đối với câu hỏi hoặc chủ đề đã cho. | Khi bạn muốn chọn những mục có nội dung thực sự liên quan nhất, bất kể thời gian hay mức độ phổ biến. |
| **recency** | Ưu tiên các mục mới nhất, dựa trên ngày xuất bản hoặc cập nhật. | Khi thời gian là yếu tố quan trọng, ví dụ: “cập nhật mới nhất về X” hoặc “tin tức hôm nay”. |
| **popularity** | Đánh giá mức độ phổ biến hoặc tương tác (likes, retweets, views, v.v.) của mục. | Khi bạn muốn tìm những nội dung được quan tâm nhiều nhất, thường dùng cho “điểm nóng” hoặc “đánh giá xu hướng”. |

> **Cách sử dụng**: Khi gọi `rank`, chỉ cần đặt `criteria` thành `"relevance"`, `"recency"` hoặc `"popularity"` tùy mục tiêu của bạn. Tool sẽ sắp xếp danh sách dựa trên tiêu chí đó và trả về `top_k` mục được chọn.

items.title: Google's chip business is on a faster track than Nvidia's own AI boom
items.summary:
Google is selling on price. SemiAnalysis found that Google's current Ironwood TPU delivers up to nearly three times as much AI output per dollar as Nvidia's Blackwell chips when running AI agents, though Nvidia's top system still wins when speed is everything.

Bar chart of peak AI computing power per chip in petaflops. Nvidia Rubin 35, Google TPU 8i Max 20, Nvidia Blackwell Ultra 15, Google TPU 8t 13, Google TPU 8i 10 and AMD MI355X 10.

Google, Nvidia, AMD, Yahoo Finance [...] Google introduced two new tensor processing units, or TPUs — its homegrown AI chips — on Monday. The TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max join the 8t and 8i it unveiled in April, the first time Google has introduced four TPU systems in a single year. Both new chips ship next year. [...] Think of it as a chip menu. The 8tx keeps data encrypted for governments, banks, and other regulated businesses, paired with processors from AMD (AMD). The 8i Max squeezes two chips into one package for requests with long context windows — the amount of information an AI model can juggle at once.

items.title: Google unveils new AI chip variants as cloud demand surges | Reuters
items.summary:
It pairs Google's chip technology with AMD's (AMD.O) processors and encrypts data ​at the hardware ​level, delivering ⁠up to twice the speed of the previous version with virtually no trade-off in performance, ​the company said.

The 8i Max, meanwhile, is designed ​for ⁠AI applications that need to process very large amounts of information at once. [...] The new chips, 8tx and 8i Max, are redesigned versions of existing processors ​tailored for specific customer needs, according to the company. Bloomberg ​News first reported the development earlier in the day.

The 8tx is aimed ‌at ⁠government agencies and companies in regulated industries that need to keep sensitive data protected while it is being processed. [...] It combines two chips into a single package to ⁠provide ​additional memory and computing power, the ​company said, making it well suited for coding assistants, mathematical reasoning and drug-discovery ​tasks.

Reporting by Anhata Rooprai in Bengaluru; Editing by Jonathan Ananda

Our Standards: The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles.

items.title: AI boom draws chip supply from other end-markets, Siltronic CEO says | Reuters
items.summary:
Demand for AI-related chips remains so strong that semiconductor manufacturers are allocating more supply to those applications, leaving less capacity for other end markets.

"When ​our customers have the choice to sell their chips to different ​segments, they will always send them to the ones that pay best," he ‌said. "The ⁠pockets of the AI players, particularly the hyperscalers, are the deepest." [...] The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

AI-linked demand has ​become the chip industry's main growth engine, but Heckmeier ​told Reuters in an interview that some other semiconductor end ⁠markets could grow faster if more chips were available.

"It's not ​that AI is offsetting certain weaknesses," Heckmeier said. "It's more AI is generating ​a certain weakness." [...] The trend has made AI servers the industry's main growth engine, with the impact extending beyond higher server volumes.

Heckmeier said AI server farms consume ​roughly three to ​four times more ⁠silicon area than traditional servers, boosting demand for advanced wafers

Any moderation in AI demand would not ​necessarily derail the industry's growth, Heckmeier said, because capacity ​could flow ⁠back to smartphones, PCs and other markets where underlying demand remains solid.

items.title: Nvidia, Chinese Espionage, and the AI Race: Four Foreign Policy Issues to Watch | Council on Foreign Relations
items.summary: Nvidia, valued at more than $4 trillion, makes the chips that underpin the large language models and data centers that have become pillars of U.S. economic growth. CFR Senior Fellow Rebecca Patterson said that Nvidia “is central to America’s AI efforts, both in terms of its size and weight in major equity indices, as well as its status as the so-called central bank for the AI ecosystem.” [...] Last year, President Donald Trump allowed Nvidia to sell H20 chips to China in exchange for a cut of the revenue, a deal later extended to the H200. However, the White House has barred the sale of Nvidia’s most advanced artificial intelligence chips—specifically its flagship Blackwell series—to China. [...] U.S. experts believe that the United States has an edge in the AI race against China. To maintain that lead, the U.S. government has barred Nvidia from selling its most cutting-edge AI chips to China since 2022. Still, critics have noted that there have been gaps in enforcing that ban. Nvidia chips can be legally sold to non-Chinese customers in other countries, such as Malaysia or Singapore, and then illicitly resold or re-exported to China. items.title: Find My AI Chips: the US Plans to Track GPUs Abroad - IEEE Spectrum
items.summary: Whether or not a “Find My” for AI chips becomes a regulatory requirement, Feldgoise envisions tighter conditions for the export of advanced AI chips. “This is based on the increasing importance of compute to national and economic security,” he says. “The chips that generate compute are being seen as a strategic resource, so I would be unsurprised if the due diligence requirements on these devices increase as time passes.” [...] To deduce an AI chip’s location, PLV measures the time it takes for a ping to travel from the chip to multiple trusted “landmark” servers around the world and back. Kyle Miller, a senior research analyst at CSET and coauthor of the report, says that for new AI chips, manufacturers could integrate PLV functionality into the hardware itself, while a firmware update could be applied to chips already in circulation. [...] Hanna Dohmen, a senior research analyst at CSET and coauthor of the report, points to other gaps in the U.S. export control regime. “Currently, Chinese companies are legally able to remotely access AI chips abroad through cloud service providers,” she says. These advanced AI chips might be installed in data centers across Southeast Asian countries like Malaysia, which are increasingly serving Chinese firms.

items.summary:
# Nvidia’s AI Chip Exports Emerge as Target in Democratic Congress

Nvidia Corp. is in for tougher scrutiny from a new Democratic majority in Congress that’s set to demand answers from Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang about whether the company is doing enough to keep its coveted artificial intelligence chips out of the hands of China and other US adversaries.
